newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean union to end all-out strikes - TV.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean union to end all-out strikes - TV.

text.p: South Korean union workers will end full strikes and stoppages will take place only once a week, Yonhap Television News reported on Saturday.
"The Korean Confederation of Trade Unions will stage stoppages only on Wednesday from next week," it said.
A spokesman of the outlawed confederation, which has been leading more than three weeks of strikes, said the group changed its tactics but details would be released later on Saturday.
He said the change was aimed at prolonging protests at a controversial labour law, which allows companies to lay off workers, replace strikers and change working hours.
The move followed pressure by the government which has vowed to crack down on wildcat strikes and arrest strike leaders.
Confederation leader Kwon Young-kil and six deputies are taking sanctuary in a Seoul cathedral as police sought to arrest them.
